text: The next morning, twenty-two days before the review, Taeo and Nib reached Ryu Survey's West practice yard: a maze of plywood screens.
Minho's sister Haein was fixing a radio. She saw Taeo's folder and took him for someone from Bluebird. Taeo explained that Chae had sent them.
Minho walked over and ordered Nib to talk. Nib said, 'You first.' Haein lit up. Minho took the correction and introduced himself properly.
Ryu Survey mapped gates before the clear teams went in. Cheaply, Haein added. Minho would vouch for Nib, but first he wanted to see what Nib could do.
The test was simple. Nib would scout, and Taeo would push a loaded trolley through the maze. The screens blocked Taeo's view, so he had to follow Nib's calls.
Haein handed out radios. Hold to talk, let go to listen. Nib called his a small shouting brick.
Nib went left and started describing the gap ahead. Taeo hit his talk button before Nib had finished. He was coming.
The trolley jammed in the gap. Nib had said he went left. He hadn't said the cart would fit.
Minho blamed Taeo for a new grey hair. Then came the actual lesson: take it back, and let Nib finish.
On the second try, Taeo kept his thumb off the button. Nib checked the long way round and reported that the right passage would fit the cart.
Taeo made it through with the load intact. Slower, Minho said. But he had finally stopped guessing.
Then Minho offered Nib a job of his own: walk the new course before his crew tomorrow. One hour, twenty thousand won, cash.
Taeo translated: two of his lunches. Nib accepted. And Minho would write a receipt for the review. Proof of work Nib had chosen himself.
Taeo asked if he could work too. Not yet, Minho said. He needed practice. He could watch.
Nib noticed Taeo sulking. He hadn't asked Minho to leave him out. Taeo knew. He had just wanted to be good at this.
Nib's advice: let him finish a sentence. Taeo laughed. Annoyingly, Nib was right.
The next morning, Nib walked the reset course alone and caught a cord strung across the exit. Minho took the warning.
Haein said Taeo looked like a dog waiting at a door. Then Minho counted two notes into Nib's hands. Both his.
For the receipt, Minho asked for his full name. Just Nib. Offered the same job next week, Nib said he would let him know.
At a noodle shop, Nib asked what a bowl cost. The server answered Taeo instead, and Taeo reached for his wallet.
Nib pushed his hand back down. 'I'm buying mine.' He solemnly offered both notes. One was enough.
Thirteen thousand won left over. Nib tasted the broth, and his ears relaxed. A meal he had paid for himself.
Grandma messaged about Sunday. Haru wanted to know when Taeo was coming, and wanted spicy seaweed snacks. Home was three hours away by bus.
Nib asked if he could come. Nobody had ever asked to come home with Taeo before. He said he would ask Grandma.
On the phone, Taeo told her he'd awakened this week and summoned a goblin. Her yell flattened Nib's ears.
Was he going into gates? No. His companion was called Nib, he talked, and he had asked to visit.
Grandma had one question. 'Does he eat fish?' He did. That settled it. Sunday, noon, both of them.
Nib reached the crossing while Taeo was still fighting his shoes. Shoes were slow, Nib observed.
A bus blocked Taeo's view down the road. Past its bumper, Nib's ear turned toward something coming.
An amber pulse hit Taeo's palm before he could see anything. He shouted Nib's name. A delivery scooter shot out from behind the bus, running the red light.
Nib sprang clear. The rider sped off, yelling an apology. Nobody was hurt.
Across the road, Taeo's hand still glowed amber. He couldn't have seen past the bus. Nib stared at him. 'You felt that. From there.'
